Misty Shot
Firearm- Pistol (rare)
This Misty Shot pistol seems to always have a small amount of smoke streaming from its barrel. This magic firearm has a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls and deals 1d8 force damage instead of piercing damage. Twice per day you may use the Misty Shot to cast Misty Step, changing the range to match the pistols range.

The Tombstone
Shield 
A tombstone broken and taken from a graveyard, the name long worn away, and only the symbol of a god can just be seen. While wielding this shield you may use Turn Undead, per Cleric rules. Turn Undead used in this way does not scale, unless used by a Cleric.

Dr. Wynn’s Herbalist Bag
Wonderous item
A leather bag, made from different animal hides and stitched together with plant fibers, the interior has numerous pockets, each with an embroidered plant on the side. This bag counts as an herbalist’s kit and gives the wielder advantage on checks to find and identify herbs.
This bag also contains 10 charges, using the herbs you may spend up to three charges as a bonus action to heal someone 1d6 hit points per charge. The charges refresh if you spend at least an hour searching for herbs or spend at least 50gp on resupplying the bag.

**Gregarious Gauntlets:**
This stall is run by a large bugbear man who talks in extremely dramatic fashion. Many of his pieces of armor are fancy and catching to the eye. He ages his whole lifespan over the course of a day, his taste and required gifts changing with him. The interior of the stall, which is an open-air blacksmithy with a small room in the back for sleeping, has several clocks strewn about. As the day progresses, the bugbear man will go by different variants of the same name: JJ, Jimmy, John, James, and Johnathan.

**Items Available:**
Barkskin Armor: Your Armor Class can't be lower than 16 while you wear this armor. It smells of sweet maple.
Stoneskin Armor: You have resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashng damage while you wear this armor. It smells of rock candy.
Coward's boots: When you take the *disengage* action on your turn, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of your turn.
Stable breastplate: The first time each day you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, this armor immediately stabilizies you at 1 hp, though you are not conscious.
Circlet of the suave: this circlet gives you advantage on saving throws against being charmed or put to sleep
Viscous armor: when an enemy rolls a natural 1 to hit you with a melee attack, they must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or have their weapon stick to you. The weapon can be removed by using an action to make a successful DC 15 Strength check. If you were hit with an appendage, the creature is grappled by you instead of being disarmed.
Shatterheart Breastplate: While wearing this breastplate, if you would be killed due to a blow/attack, instead the armor takes the hit for you and is destroyed, infusing you with enough life essence to be conscious at 1HP, albeit without armor.
Two-faced Helmet: While wearing this helmet, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) and cannot be surprised unless you are blinded.
(This is all obviously subject to approval from <@!592252026226999306>  in regards to the items)

**Paddy's Pub**
Situated on the south corner of the Western Hilltop park, this pub made of stone and wood is split down the middle and has two entrances: one on the feywild bleed side, and one that leads out into the more mundane section of The Bustle. There are no rules or firm divisions between the two sides, and mingling occurs frequently. Uncle Paddy is an older Kimellian man who speaks with a somewhat Irish accent. (Does this make sense? kinda, i guess?) Paddy is keen to offer advice to newcomers, as well as drinks and various potions. The drinks come in both alcoholic and non-alcoholic versions. One of the foods that is sold is a sugary grain cereal, marketed by someone who is in opposition to Kellog. To-go orders are allowed, but **all drinks bought at the pub will spoil the following dawn, becoming inert (albeit still alcoholic).**
The interior of the bar appears more slanted and uneven the more you approach the fey side, making it difficult not to spill your drink.

**Items Available:**
Airhead ale: This drink makes you feel light of both head and body. For the next hour, you levitate 5ft off of the ground at your walking speed, and descend at a rate of 5ft every 30ft if more than 5ft off of the ground. However, you find it hard to focus, and have disadvantage on saving throws to maintain concentration. 60gp.
Begger's Bottle: This drink allows you to use the "Grovel and Beg" racial feature of Kobolds once in the next hour. 130gp.
Banshee's Brew: This dark grey drink seems to wail mournfully at a low volume. When drunk, you can emit a mournful wail. ALL creatures within 30 feet of you must make a wisdom saving throw or take psychic damage equal to 2d8 plus your Charisma modifier. If you warn your allies ahead of time, they have advantage on this saving throw. 135gp.
Cizzle Cider: This drink container is home to a small fire elemental, and can either be drank to give you resistance to fire damage for the next ten minutes, or can be smashed against the ground, causing each creature within 10 feet of the item to make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take 14 (4d6) fire damage. 250gp.
The Floral Ferment: This drink is sweet-smelling and enticing, giving you advantage on persuasion and deception checks for the next hour due to the sweet smell and charming demeanor it gives the drinker. 110gp.

Grasping Guinness: When drank, this beverage makes your unarmed strikes have a reach of 15 feet and pull the target up to 10 feet closer to you on a successful hit as your arms elongate and become rubbery for the next hour. 185gp.
Lurching Leprechaun: This drink is constantly swirling and moving in the container. When drank, you gain the ability to take the *disengage* action as a bonus action as you sway around unpredictably. You also gain the ability to stand up from prone using only 5 feet of movement. These benefits last for 1 hour. 80 gp.
Troublemaker's Tankard: When drank, this large tankard of popping ale gives you the ability to cast the *minor illusion* cantrip as a bonus action for the next hour. 150 gp.
Wine of Whimsy: This dark purple drink made from grapes causes the drinker to giggle for the next hour when not otherwise speaking, making them seem like less of a threat. Attacks against you have disadvantage if you have not damaged an enemy or used a negative effect on one this combat. 70 gp.

This is the story of how Johnathan Chapman turned The City (Manhattan) into a solar punk borough.
Act 1.
Johnathan, a druid sees the great fire of New York. He, being a wildfire druid is worried about his apprentice who left for the city some time ago.
Act 2. 
His investigations lead him to find that his apprentice is dead, and despite learning that his body was found at the scene of the crime, he has been burnt to death by non magical means. The true culprits are a group called New Amsterdam, a group of the oldest families in New York- rich dutch Auctioneers. 
Act 3.
Johnathan follow the trail through Broadway and wall street where he makes allies with the elves who will someday become the dominate force in Manhattan who also need to drive out the insidious force of New Amsterdam.
